Our vision is to transform how the world uses information to enrich life for all.

Micron Technology is a world leader in innovating memory and storage solutions that accelerate the transformation of information into intelligence, inspiring the world to learn, communicate and advance faster than ever.

We validate Micron memory products on current and next-generation computing platforms. As an Intern System Compatibility Engineer, you will join our System Enablement and Test Development teams and gain hands-on experience with platform bring-up, system configuration, memory validation, test development, automation, data analysis, and AI-enabled engineering workflows under the guidance of experienced engineers.

We will provide technical mentorship, structured onboarding, and exposure to DRAM, BIOS and firmware interactions, computer architecture, laboratory workflows, responsible use of approved AI tools, and the memory product lifecycle from initial bring-up through qualification and readiness.

Key Responsibilities

- Set up and support Intel, AMD, and ARM-based systems in Linux, Windows, and UEFI environments; document hardware, BIOS, firmware, operating system, memory, and test configurations for repeatable execution and traceability.

- Implement memory validation activities that assess compatibility, stability, reliability, performance, and platform readiness.
- Reproduce and triage failures, collect logs and diagnostic data, use issue-tracking systems, apply structured failure-analysis methods, and support validation of corrective actions.
- Build or refine automation using Python, PowerShell, C++, or related languages; use approved AI-assisted tools to accelerate code development, test generation, log analysis, data summarization, technical research, documentation, and reporting while applying engineering judgment to verify accuracy and results.
- Apply responsible AI practices by protecting confidential information, using company-approved tools and data sources, documenting AI-assisted work where appropriate, identifying potential errors or bias, and independently validating generated code, analysis, and technical conclusions before use.
- Collaborate with System Enablement, Test Engineering, product, quality, and program teams on assigned validation and root-cause investigation activities.
- Communicate findings, risks, dependencies, corrective actions, and recommended next steps through concise documentation and presentations.
- Internship Assignment - The intern will complete a bounded technical project or workstream with defined milestones, measurable deliverables, technical documentation, and a final presentation. The assignment will be selected to provide relevant business value while remaining achievable within a three-month summer internship!

Required Qualifications

- Currently pursuing a bachelor’s or graduate degree in Computer Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Computer Science, or a closely related technical field. Must be continuing education in the fall term following the internship; the expected graduation date must not be before September of the same year.
- Foundational knowledge of computer hardware, operating systems, computer architecture, and structured problem-solving.

- Programming or scripting experience gained through coursework, projects, laboratories, student organizations, or other technical experience using Python, PowerShell, C++, or a comparable language.
- Basic proficiency using AI-enabled tools to research technical topics, develop or solve code, analyze data, summarize findings, or improve documentation, with the ability to review outputs critically and confirm accuracy.
- Ability to follow test procedures, maintain accurate configuration records, analyze data, and summarize technical results. Interest in hands-on laboratory validation, system debug, test development, or engineering automation.

Preferred Qualifications

- Experience working with DRAM, memory systems, BIOS or UEFI, firmware, server or client platforms, or hardware interfaces.

- Familiarity with x86 or ARM architectures, Intel, AMD, ARM-based, or embedded platforms, and Linux, Windows, or UEFI environments.
- Experience with oscilloscopes, logic analyzers, protocol analyzers, power measurement equipment, or similar diagnostic tools.
- Experience applying generative AI, machine learning, automation, or data-analysis tools to an engineering or academic workflow—for example, developing code, generating tests, analyzing logs, identifying patterns, creating dashboards, improving documentation, or automating repetitive tasks.

Who We Are

GITAI is a vertically integrated space and defense company building the next generation of hardware for low-Earth-orbit missions.

At our core is the space robotics technology that has defined GITAI from the beginning. A small, highly capable engineering team applies that foundation across satellite buses, in-orbit servicing robotics, and mission hardware for applications such as Earth observation. Today, a major focus of our work is supporting U.S. national security missions, particularly through proliferated LEO satellite constellations and other next-generation space systems.

We design, build, integrate, and test much of our hardware in-house. Electrical, mechanical, software, manufacturing, integration, and test teams work closely together, allowing a small team to own complete systems rather than isolated components. This vertical integration helps us move quickly, learn directly from hardware, and shorten the path from architecture to a working system.

We are still early. The systems, the company, and the market are all being built at the same time. Requirements change, technical problems are often ambiguous, and many answers do not yet exist. We are looking for exceptional engineers and operators who want broad ownership, can work across disciplines, and are willing to stay close to the hardware until the mission succeeds.

Your Mission

As a Field-Deployed Software Engineering Intern, you will support the development, integration, and testing of GITAI’s robotic and space systems. A major part of this role happens on real hardware. You will regularly deploy to our outdoor test site to support data acquisition, system bring-up, troubleshooting, and test execution. You will also contribute to software development in at least one technical area such as robotics, computer vision, or guidance, navigation, and control (GNC). You should be comfortable moving between code, sensors, computers, networks, actuators, and test equipment to understand why a system is or is not working.

What You’ll Drive

- Support weekly field testing, including system setup, bring-up, data acquisition, logging, monitoring, and troubleshooting.

- Develop and debug software for robotics, computer vision, GNC, or related systems.

- Diagnose problems across software and hardware, including sensors, actuators, communications, timing, configuration, and computing systems.

- Build scripts and lightweight tools for data collection, visualization, system health monitoring, and test automation.

- Review test data and logs, reproduce failures, and work with engineers to identify root causes and fixes.

- Support hardware/software integration and test preparation at our Torrance facility between field deployments.

- Document test configurations, issues, findings, and software changes so the engineering team can act on them quickly.

What We’re Looking For

- Currently pursuing or recently completed a BS or MS in Computer Science, Robotics, Electrical Engineering, Aerospace Engineering, or a related technical field.

- At least 1 year of sustained, hands-on contribution to a robotics team, rocketry team, Formula SAE, research lab, or a similar environment where software was developed, integrated, and debugged on physical hardware.

- Available to work at least three days per week.

- Able to spend Wednesdays and Thursdays at GITAI’s outdoor test site in the desert region near Los Angeles on a regular basis.

- Hands-on experience getting software to work with real hardware through internships, research, student teams, competitions, or personal projects.

- Experience in at least one of the following areas: robotics, computer vision, controls, GNC, autonomy, or embedded systems.

- Experience programming in Python or C++.

- Comfortable working in Linux.

- Strong debugging skills and the ability to work through problems that cross software and hardware boundaries.

- Comfortable working outdoors around active engineering test operations.

- U.S. citizenship required, as this role may support U.S. Government programs that require eligibility for a U.S. Secret security clearance.

Strong Plus:

- Experience with ROS or ROS 2.

- Experience integrating sensors, cameras, actuators, embedded computers, or robotic systems.

- Experience with OpenCV, PyTorch, state estimation, motion planning, control systems, or related robotics software.

- Experience with hardware communication interfaces such as CAN, Ethernet, serial, EtherCAT, or similar protocols.

- Experience with data acquisition, telemetry, time synchronization, or analysis of experimental test data.

Location & Employment Details

- Location: Torrance, CA (onsite). Frequent overnight travel to desert test sites, including Barstow, Mojave, and other locations throughout Southern California, is expected based on program needs.

- Employment Type: Part-time, temporary, non-exempt

- Compensation: $28 - $40 per hour. Final compensation will be determined based on academic level, relevant technical experience, and demonstrated hands-on engineering capability.

- Typical Work Hours: Monday to Friday, approximately 9:00am – 6:00pm (onsite). Flexibility is expected based on mission schedules and program needs.

GITAI does not accept unsolicited resumes from staffing or recruiting agencies. We work only with recruiting partners that have been specifically engaged by GITAI. No fees will be paid for resumes submitted without a prior agreement.

Important Notice

- Applicants must be currently authorized to work in the U.S. This role is not eligible for visa sponsorship.

- To conform to U.S. Government space technology export regulations, including the International Traffic in Arms Regulations (ITAR), GITAI Employees must be a U.S. citizen, lawful U.S. permanent resident (i.e., current Green Card holder), or lawfully admitted into the U.S. as a refugee or granted asylum, or be eligible to obtain the required authorizations from the U.S. Department of State and/or the U.S. Department of Commerce, as applicable.

- GITAI USA is an Equal Opportunity Employer. Employment with GITAI USA is governed on the basis of merit, competence and qualifications and will not be influenced in any manner by race, color, religion, gender, national origin/ethnicity, veteran status, disability status, age, sexual orientation, gender identity, marital status, mental or physical disability or any other legally protected status.

About Instead

Instead is where tax work gets done. Our AI agent orchestrates the entirety of how work gets done in tax, from preparation and compliance to filing and advisory. It's a fundamentally new way of doing tax work, and it's why top 500 firms, Big Four teams, and enterprise corporate tax departments are choosing Instead.

What makes us unique: we hold full government approvals with the IRS, 48 states, and all cities to e-file 1040, 1041, 1120, 1120S, and 1065, with 706, 709, 990, 5500, 2290, and PPT coming for tax year 2026. Instead is a full replacement for CCH Axcess, GoSystem, UltraTax, OneSource, CorpTax, Lacerte, ProConnect, Drake, and more. No other tax startup will be able to offer these capabilities for years as we are two to three years ahead of everyone else in government approvals. This lets us build product experiences that are simply unmatched in the market.

Instead is backed by Conviction, IRIS (the largest tax software provider in the UK), Skylark, Aprio, and many of our partners and customers. Our team includes leaders from Intuit, Gusto, Zenefits, Thomson Reuters, Wolters Kluwer, PwC, BDO, RSM, and KPMG.

The Role

We're looking for Software Engineering Interns to join our San Francisco team and build real features on our AI-powered tax platform. This is not a coffee-fetching internship. You'll ship production code that hundreds of accounting firms use, work alongside senior engineers, and get hands-on experience building with AI tools from day one.

Our stack: Vue, Nuxt, TypeScript, and Tailwind CSS on the frontend. Go, Docker on AWS ECS/Fargate, and PostgreSQL on AWS RDS on the backend. For AI, we use Cursor, Claude Code, Helicone, Gemini, and OpenAI, and we're constantly evaluating new tools.

What You'll Do

- Ship product features end to end on our live customer platform alongside senior engineers

- Build and test AI-powered components including inference pipelines and prompt engineering

- Fix bugs and make product improvements based on real customer feedback

- Create internal tools that make the engineering team more productive

- Learn our full stack and contribute across frontend, backend, and AI layers

- Participate in code reviews, architecture discussions, and product planning

What You Bring

- Currently pursuing or recently completed a degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering, or a related field

- Strong programming fundamentals. You can write clean code, debug efficiently, and think about edge cases

- Familiarity with web development (frontend or backend). Experience with any modern framework counts

- Curiosity about AI and willingness to learn. Experience with AI coding tools (Cursor, Claude Code, GitHub Copilot) is a plus

- High attention to detail and a bias for shipping

- Ability to work on-site in San Francisco

What Makes Someone Exceptional

- You've built and shipped side projects or open-source contributions that demonstrate your ability to go from idea to working product

- You already use AI tools in your coding workflow and understand how they change the way software gets built

- You learn fast and don't wait to be told what to do. When you see something broken, you fix it

- You care about the end user, not just the code. You want to understand why something matters before you build it

- You're excited about working at a startup where your work ships to real customers on day one

Location

San Francisco (on-site)

Instead is an equal opportunity employer. We evaluate candidates based on capability, judgment, ownership, and fit for the role's responsibilities. We welcome candidates who can help us build a category-defining company in tax technology.

OVERVIEW:

At DICK’S Sporting Goods, we believe in how positively sports can change lives. On our team, everyone plays a critical role in creating confidence and excitement by personally equipping all athletes to achieve their dreams. We are committed to creating an inclusive and diverse workforce, reflecting the communities we serve.

If you are ready to make a difference as part of the world’s greatest sports team, apply to join our team today!

We take a people-centric approach to everything we do. Our Athletes, how we refer to customers, and our Teammates, how we refer to our employees, are at the center of every decision we make so that we can provide transformational experiences online, in store, and in sport. When you join the Technology team as an Intern at DICK’S Sporting Goods, you’re joining a true team that wins together. We help our Athletes and fellow Teammates better their best by innovating solutions to interesting business problems and empowering every Technology Teammate to be an innovator. And, while our broader Technology team works remotely from all over the United States, they provide virtual and in-person events for the team to hangout, from virtual escape rooms to cheering on the Pittsburgh Pirates at beautiful PNC Park. As a DICK’S Sporting Goods Technology Intern, you will spend your Summer in Pittsburgh working at our Customer Support Center (our Corporate Office)! We follow a hybrid work schedule, in the office Tuesday – Thursday and working from home (your apartment) Monday and Friday.

DSG’s Technology Interns work with and learn from the leaders who bring our vision to the Best Sports Company in the World to life. During the 11-week Summer experience, interns are assigned a strategic project that is selected by a leader on their Technology team. At the conclusion of the summer, you will present your project directly to your leadership team. As a bonus to our program, you will have regular Q&A sessions with senior leaders, take part in a visit to our multiple store banners, and interact with teammates across the organization including networking and volunteer opportunities.

To support you throughout the Summer, we have built a strong support system of managers and mentors. For project guidance and day-to-day management, you will be paired with a Training Manager. Additionally, you will have status-checks and coaching from both leaders in our Technology Department and our University Relations Team. You will also have peer mentorship from Technology teammates earlier in their career. This support structure will aid in transitioning you to the DSG team, the exploration of your career goals, and will provide opportunities to develop professional and social networks within the company and the retail industry.

The experiential learning you will receive enables you to rapidly become a contributing member of the team, while also focusing on your own personal development. If you join DSG, you will have the opportunity to be a part of an enthusiastic and supportive team culture, be challenged to make a meaningful difference in our business decisions, and get a peek behind the curtain of how a large company thinks about its growth strategies.

As a Product Management Intern, you will look to discover, understand, and communicate product management methodologies and frameworks to create intuitive, loveable products. Interns will work in a fast-paced, lean environment, collaborating closely with other interns, as well as full-time Product designers, product managers, and software engineers.

We are looking for people with hybrid talents who are curious, passionate about problem solving, and can drive successful product outcomes in support of our customers and the business.

Key Responsibilities:

Strategy – You will learn the following while working with a Product Management coach:

• Use data to identify customer pain points
• Participate in sessions to identify the right problems
• Participate in prioritizing problems for best business outcomes
• Gather & analyze market data inclusive of creating competitive analyses, bench market or SWOT presentations
• Participate in identifying patterns in data & build expanded research models
• Create & present reports on findings, defects, improvements, statuses & risk management
• Use decision support tools to weigh the competing factors for prioritization of backlog
• Contribute to team discovery efforts

Execution – You will learn the following while working on a Product Team

• Tasked with key projects & provides support to more senior-level Product Managers
• Scoping & prioritization of tasks that are assigned to you
• Perform validation for production releases, bug fixes & feature requests
• Troubleshoot defects, participate in root cause analysis & find solutions for resolution
• Work on specific features, improving them & creating new ones upon instruction
• Participate in Agile ceremonies, including planning, grooming, demos & retrospectives
• Write user stories to articulate work to be done by Engineering that support outcome delivery
• Work closely with engineering to ensure delivery of products map to customer experience & business requirements within needed timelines

Key Deliverables of a Product Manager at DICK’S Sporting Goods

• Stakeholder Relationship Management
• Competitive Gap Analysis & Benchmarking
• Product Data Analysis & Reporting
• Writing & Grooming User Stories
• User Acceptance Testing

Some of your experiences will include:

• Multi-day intern orientation to introduce you to the company, the program, Pittsburgh, and your teammates
• Professional development workshops designed to increase your knowledge of the company and the retail industry, as well as develop your business acumen and office professionalism
• Extensive exposure to our senior leadership through our exclusive intern only Executive Speaker Series which includes a private meet & greet with our CEO
• Opportunities to “live the brand” and experience summer fun outside the office through various events
• Working a 40-hour work week, Monday – Friday

Skills we are looking for:

• A foundational understanding of Product Management
• Ability to balance business objectives and customer needs
• Strong deductive reasoning skills
• A customer-centric view into developing great product experiences
• Ability to distill complex technical concepts into plain language for stakeholders
• Strong curiosity when it comes to using new tools, adopting new technology, and learning new product management frameworks that will progress your professional development
• Dynamic written and verbal communication style, as well as the ability to communicate cross-functionally and vertically throughout the organization
• Knowledge of Agile methodologies
• Ability to work in a fast-paced and outcome-oriented environment

We look for potential candidates with:

• Attending an accredited university, college or technical school
• Graduation date of Winter 2027 or Spring 2028
• An undergrad or Master’s degree in Product Management, Business, Technology or related field

Internship Start Date: May 17th 2027
Internship End Date: July 29th 2027

Full-time opportunities in 2028:

Interns qualified for full-time opportunities will be evaluated at the end of the program. Qualified interns will be placed into a full-time Technology Development Program.

Perks:

- Consideration for full-time jobs after graduation*

- Fully furnished housing for non-local interns arranged and paid for by DSG

- Hybrid work model: WFH Monday & Friday, in office Tues – Thurs.

- Two paid holidays – Memorial Day and July 4th

- Teammate Discount

- Uber codes for Interns who do not have a vehicle to commute to and from the office

- Corporate Office amenities such as on-site gym and Starbucks

- Meaningful work projects selected by functional leaders

- Executive Speaker Series

- Professional development

- Volunteer opportunities

- Social events such as Intern Olympics, a Pittsburgh Pirates game, National Intern Day celebration, and more!

*Relocation assistance will be provided for non-local candidates who accept full-time jobs requiring them to be located at DICK’S Sporting Goods Corporate Office

Here’s what a few of our 2025 Interns had to say:

“At DSG, we don’t just identify challenges but have the opportunity to shape the solutions. Knowing that my voice matters and my work drives real impact across the company has been incredibly empowering. If you’re willing to show up and put in the work, DSG will grow you in ways you never thought possible.” – Kelsey Riemer, People & Purpose Intern

“During my internship at DSG, what I loved most was the incredible opportunity to immerse myself in a company that is not only large and well-established, but also rapidly growing and constantly evolving. As someone interested in the retail industry, it was great to be part of such a dynamic environment allowed me to develop deep expertise in my role, gain hands-on experience, and see firsthand how continuous improvement in all areas drives the company forward.” – Jackson Lopiano, Retail Analytics Intern

“My internship at DICK’S Sporting Goods was an incredible experience. I loved being part of a team that truly values collaboration, growth, and innovation. One of the best parts was getting to meet other interns and learn about different areas of the business. It gave me a much deeper understanding of how everything connects. I also appreciated how immersed I was in the DICK’S culture from day one. It’s a place where people are passionate about what they do, and that energy is contagious. I felt supported, challenged, and inspired throughout the entire program.” – Kristin Bayuk, Finance Intern

“My internship experience at Dick’s Sporting Goods was incredibly rewarding. - Cybersecurity: Combination of people, policies, processes, and technologies employed by an enterprise to protect its cyber assets

About Zipline

Zipline is the world’s largest and most experienced drone delivery service. We are on a mission to serve all humans equally by ensuring access to food, medicine and essential goods anytime, anywhere. We design, build, and operate the world’s largest autonomous logistics system, delivering critical supplies quickly and reliably. Today, Zipline operates on four continents, makes a delivery somewhere in the world every 30 seconds, and has completed millions of deliveries to date, including blood, vaccines, medical supplies, food, and retail products.

Our customers include the world’s largest and most prominent healthcare systems, governments, retailers, restaurants and global businesses who rely on us to save lives, reduce emissions, increase economic opportunity, and provide delivery from point A to point B as fast as possible. The drone is only 15% of what we’ve built to enable seamless, reliable, global operations.

Our system strengthens supply chains, reduces congestion, and gives people time back. With more than 140 million commercial autonomous miles safely flown, Zipline is redefining access to healthcare, consumer products, and food across the globe.

We operate at a global scale and are looking for practical problem solvers who thrive on real-world challenges and rapid growth. Our team is motivated by building systems that have a direct, meaningful impact on people’s lives and by scaling the future of logistics. We are seeking people who sculpt from first principles, enjoy facing adversity, and can do the impossible at record breaking speeds.

About the Global Supply Management Team

The Global Supply Management Team ensures that Zipline has the parts it needs from suppliers around the world in a reliable, sustainable, and cost-effective way. We build and maintain strong relationships with suppliers, negotiate contracts, and monitor supplier performance to reduce supply risk. The team also works closely with the design engineering, supplier industrial engineering, finance, program management, and material management teams to understand part design, manage supply against demand, drive cost reductions, and streamline logistics across international markets.

The Role

As a Global Supply Management Intern, you’ll gain hands-on exposure to the systems, data, and supplier relationships that power Zipline’s global supply chain. You’ll work alongside supply managers, engineers, finance, and operations teams to support sourcing, analytics, and day-to-day execution. This role is perfect for a student to apply classroom knowledge to real-world challenges in procurement, logistics, and global operations.

Your work will directly support Zipline’s mission to deliver essential goods and services across the world while building critical skills in supply chain management.

What You'll Do

- Assist in tracking and analyzing supplier performance, purchase orders, and delivery timelines.

- Prepare reports, dashboards, and presentations on supply chain metrics.

- Support sourcing activities by gathering quotes, conducting supplier research, and benchmarking costs.

- Work with internal stakeholders to troubleshoot supply issues and identify process improvements.

- Participate in supplier meetings and cross-functional discussions to gain exposure to real-world negotiations and decision-making.

- Document and standardize processes to help build scalable systems.

What You'll Bring

- Currently pursuing a Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Supply Chain Management, Engineering, Business, Economics, or a related field.

- Strong analytical and problem-solving skills; comfortable working with spreadsheets (Excel/Google Sheets).

- Curiosity and eagerness to learn about global supply chain operations in a fast-paced environment.

- Strong communication and collaboration skills, with the ability to work on cross-functional projects.

- Organizational skills and attention to detail, with a willingness to dive into both strategic and tactical tasks.

What Else You Should Know

Our internships are full-time positions, in-person at our South San Francisco office. We will host our Spring 2027 interns from January 2027 to April/May 2027.

Candidates are limited to three (3) applications within a 30-day period.

Zipline is an equal opportunity employer and prohibits discrimination and harassment of any type without regard to race, color, religion, age, sex, national origin, disability status, genetics, protected veteran status, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, or any other characteristic protected by federal, state or local laws or our own sensibilities.

Zipline is also committed to providing reasonable accommodations to individuals with disabilities. Please let your point of contact at Zipline know if you require any accommodations throughout your interview process.

Voluntary Self-Identification

For government reporting purposes, we ask candidates to respond to the below self-identification survey. Completion of the form is entirely voluntary. Whatever your decision, it will not be considered in the hiring process or thereafter. Any information that you do provide will be recorded and maintained in a confidential file.

- Verify marketing campaign information for uploading to our internal platforms.
- Create and edit paid advertising and promotional campaigns.
- Assist Marketing Analytics team members on ad-hoc research and analysis projects.

- Effective communication skills and ability to prioritize projects based on business needs

- Creative experience with Canva and in-app image and video editing (e.g. Tiktok, Instagram) a plus
- Working knowledge of the publishing industry a plus
- A knowledge and passion for books and reading

- This position will be a hybrid of remote work and in-office attendance (at least 2 days a week in the New York City office will be required).

Aluminum Dynamics

Overview

What Does Steel Dynamics Do?

Steel Dynamics is a leading industrial metals solutions company that produces lower-carbon, high-quality steel products primarily from recycled scrap. Operating through a circular manufacturing model, the company manufactures a wide range of steel products including flat roll, structural, and long products for industries such as construction, automotive, energy, and manufacturing. In addition to steel production, Steel Dynamics operates metals recycling facilities, steel fabrication plants, and aluminum production operations, serving customers across North America with a focus on innovation, efficiency, and sustainability.

This is an Aluminum Dynamics (ADL) Internship. What Does ADL Do?

Aluminum Dynamics is developing a state-of-the-art, 650,000-tonne low-carbon recycled aluminum flat rolled mill, supported by two satellite recycled aluminum slab centers. The facility will produce a wide range of flat rolled aluminum products while prioritizing sustainability through advanced recycling practices. Our product offering includes value-added finishing lines such as Continuous Annealing and Solution Heat treatment (CASH) lines, continuous coating, and multiple slitting and packaging operations. This combination of cutting-edge technology and sustainable processes positions Aluminum Dynamics as a leader in delivering high-quality, low-carbon aluminum solutions to meet the growing demands of diverse industries.

What Makes This Internship Different?

This internship is unique compared to other software development internships because instead of creating software to be sold to external companies, interns at SDI develop and debug applications that directly serve our internal customers. This means interns work closely with employees across the company, particularly those in operations, to understand their day-to-day needs and challenges. By building software that improves internal processes and supports SDI’s workforce, interns gain firsthand experience in creating practical solutions while developing strong relationships with internal customers. This direct interaction not only strengthens communication and problem-solving skills but also provides valuable insight into how technology supports a large-scale manufacturing environment.

Internship Location

This internship is located at Aluminum Dynamics located in Columbus, MS. This internship will take place during the Summer 2027 term.

Internship Benefits

- Furnished Housing Free of Cost

- Provided for interns living more than 50 miles from their work site, including essential furnishings to ensure a comfortable stay during the internship.

- 401(k) & Company Match

- Eligibility to participate in the company 401(k) plan with a 10–50% company match that vests immediately.

- Employee Discounts

- Access to discounts on hotels, vehicles, and other goods and services through Steel Dynamics’ nationwide partner network.

- Employee Assistance Program

- Up to five free visits per issue, per year for counseling, legal advice, financial guidance, and other daily living resources.

- Intern Extravaganza

- A two-day event at company headquarters featuring facility tours, networking with company leaders, cultural immersion, and connecting with other interns from across the country.

- Competitive Pay

- Competitive hourly wages for all internship positions, rewarding the value interns bring to the company.

Responsibilities

What Are My Responsibilities as a Software Development Intern at Aluminum Dynamics?

- Participate in real-world software development projects alongside experienced developers, contributing to applications used across the company.

- Review, analyze, and modify software applications, including coding, testing, debugging, and documenting.

- Build and enhance internal web applications using technologies such as C#, HTML, Blazor, Microsoft SQL, and Microsoft Azure.

- Design and implement new features and functionality to improve user experience, navigation, and system performance.

- Collaborate with team members in Agile-style development meetings, assisting with project planning, task division, code reviews, and integration of updates.

- Support software users by assisting with bug fixes, troubleshooting, training, and IT-related requests.

- Gain exposure to the full software development lifecycle, from planning and prototyping to coding, testing, debugging, and deployment.

Qualifications

What Qualifications Do I Need?

- Pursuing a Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering, Information Technology, or a related field

- Preferred GPA of 2.7 or higher

- Foundational knowledge of programming languages such as C#, HTML, and SQL

- Familiarity with web development frameworks such as .NET/TypeScript is a plus

- Understanding of database management and query writing

- Strong problem-solving and analytical skills

- Ability to work independently and as part of a collaborative development team

- Effective communication skills, both written and verbal

- Detail-oriented with the ability to follow coding standards and documentation practices

- Interest in learning Agile development practices and the full software development lifecycle

Examples of Projects Steel Dynamics Software Development Interns Have Completed

- Participate in a real-world software development internship, working directly with experienced developers to contribute to live internal applications used across the company.

- Build and enhance a Blazor-based web application called the Picnic Project, using C#, HTML, and Microsoft SQL to manage company events, registrations, and attendee tracking.

- Design and implement new functionality such as event duplication templates, calendar integration, map displays, and enhanced user navigation for improved interface experience.

- Create, modify, and optimize SQL queries and C# scripts to streamline data retrieval and reporting functions, supporting both backend logic and frontend application behavior.

- Improve system security by contributing to login security features and managing access protocols for company-wide applications.

About Base

Base is America’s next-generation power company. We’re rebuilding the foundation of modern civilization–electricity–by deploying a vast network of distributed batteries that is transforming today’s fragile, centralized grid into a resilient and abundant system. We are engineers, operators, and creatives solving some of the most complex, interdisciplinary challenges of our time.

About the Role

We are seeking an intern to join Base’s Business Operations team that focuses on commercial partnerships. During your internship you’ll be tasked with important problems for the business and expected to deliver just like any other full-time member of the team.

In this role, you’ll help launch new growth-oriented partnerships, support existing partner operations, and improve financial and operational processes across the business. That means driving volume growth, unit economics, and quality outcomes while ensuring our partner stays motivated to win alongside us. At Base, partnerships aren’t siloed – you’ll collaborate closely with Deployments, Growth, Software, and Hardware to deliver results that matter.

What You’ll Do

- Our Business Operations team is lean and has a broad scope; there are many specific opportunities awaiting you if you have a thoughtful and effective approach.

- Support our relationships and overall offering to existing business partners.

- Build analytical tools to understand our operational and financial performance, uncover opportunities for efficiency or growth, and provide visibility to the Base team on critical information.

- Automate operational processes to more efficiently support our members and deployments growth.

- Launch and scale new partnership programs from 0 to 1.

What You'll Bring

- Comfort working with modern tools and tech stack (e.g., Python, SQL, dashboards, CRMs) and rolling up your sleeves when needed.

- Analytical and data-driven mindset to decision-making and sound business judgment to determine project performance and financial viability.

- Excellent written and verbal communication skills.

- Proficiency in Powerpoint/Slides and Excel.

- Proficiency in one or more programming languages is a plus.

- Bias toward action and simplification - constantly pushing toward alignment, clarity, and execution on tight timelines.

- Comfortable with ambiguity and effective prioritization in a fast paced entrepreneurial environment.

About the Team

The Base business operations team is responsible for some of the company's highest-leverage outcomes: financing our growth, commercial partnerships, acquisitions and integrations, new market and product entries, and the programs that span too many teams to have a natural owner. It is a set of small teams of generalists who work directly with Base's founders, pick up the problem that matters most, build the structure and analysis it needs, and hand back something that runs itself.

Please note: Base is a startup, which means priorities shift and evolve quickly. Your role may expand or change based on the needs of the business at any given time, so the responsibilities listed may not be exhaustive.

Our Values

- First Principles Thinking: Question assumptions. Principles > rules.

- Operate at Base Pace: Focus on what matters, act quickly, and learn by doing.

- Give & Get Feedback: Be direct, be humble, and maintain a growth mindset.

- Everyone’s an Owner: Follow through on commitments and own results.

- Strong Opinions, Loosely Held: Drive clarity and make calls with imperfect information.

- Committed to the Mission: Rebuilding the grid is a big challenge. We work hard because we care deeply about the impact we’re creating. We work in-person. It’s not a 9-to-5. We are all-in.

- Fun & Optimism Coexist with Grit: Collaboration and celebration coincide with the intensity of building real things.

Do the best work of your life at Base.

SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of enabling human life on Mars.

SPRING 2027 SOFTWARE ENGINEERING INTERNSHIP/CO-OP

SpaceX seeks extraordinary students to join us for software engineering roles in Spring 2027. As a software intern, you will work closely with your mentor and other employees who will help you apply your knowledge and grow your skills on projects that have a significant impact. You’ll also get to have some fun and network with other interns and employees through optional social and professional events. If you’ve demonstrated a commitment to academic success and motivation to apply your knowledge outside of the classroom, you are a great candidate! Aerospace experience is not required to be successful here - rather we look for smart, motivated, collaborative engineers who love solving problems and want to make an impact on a super inspiring mission.

Internships are available with a variety of software engineering teams across the company at Bastrop, TX; Brownsville, TX; Cape Canaveral, FL; Hawthorne (Los Angeles), CA; Irvine, CA; McGregor (Waco), TX; Palo Alto, CA; and Redmond (Seattle), WA.

BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:

- Must be enrolled in a bachelor’s degree or graduate program

- 3+ months of software programming or development experience

- Software coding experience in one or more of the following: C, C++, C#, Java, JavaScript, Python

- Applicant for this intern position must be a (i) U.S. citizen or national, (ii) U.S. lawful permanent resident (e.g., green card holder), (iii) Refugee under 8 U.S.C. § 1157, or (iv) Asylee under 8 U.S.C. § 1158.

PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:

- GPA of 3.5 or above

- 6+ months experience developing and deploying software that has been used on real-world applications and projects

- Strong fundamental knowledge of computer architecture and networks

- Experience with software documentation, creating system diagrams, and enumerating software requirements

- Strong skills in debugging, performance optimization and unit testing

- Strong interpersonal skills (examples: leading a student organization or working successfully in teams)

- Ability to work effectively in a dynamic environment with changing needs and requirements

- Ability to work independently and in a team, take initiative, and communicate effectively

ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS:

- Able to work full time, onsite for a minimum of 12 consecutive weeks beginning in January or March 2027

- Able to provide own transportation for positions at Brownsville, Cape Canaveral and McGregor locations

COMPENSATION AND BENEFITS:

Pay Range:

Software Engineering Intern/Freshman/Sophomore: $30.00/hour
Software Engineering Intern/Junior/Senior: $34.00/hour
Software Engineering Intern/Completed Bachelor's: $36.00/hour
Software Engineering Intern/Completed Master's: $38.00/hour
Software Engineering Intern/Completed PhD: $40.00/hour

Your salary will be determined by academic level. Pay is just one part of your total rewards package at SpaceX. You may also be eligible for a stipend to subsidize relocation costs, as well as access to our comprehensive medical coverage and a 401(k) retirement plan. Students joining SpaceX through our internship program will receive the opportunity to attend presentations from company leaders, social and networking events, as well as professional and personal development trainings. Interns are also eligible for paid company holidays. SpaceX offers 10 or more paid holidays per year.

PROGRAM DESCRIPTIONS:

VEHICLE

- DRAGON: The Dragon spacecraft is capable of carrying up to 7 passengers to and from Earth orbit, and beyond. It is the only spacecraft currently flying that is capable of returning significant amounts of cargo to Earth and is the first private spacecraft to take humans to the space station.

- FALCON: The Falcon program tackles space exploration’s toughest problems through the ongoing development of our reusable launch vehicles, Falcon 9 and Falcon Heavy. These vehicles are currently responsible for delivering commercial, national security, and NASA satellites into orbit, as well as supply critical science, supplies, and crew to the International Space Station.

- STARSHIP: The Starship spacecraft and Super Heavy rocket – collectively referred to as Starship – represent a fully reusable transportation system designed to carry both crew and cargo to Earth orbit, the Moon, Mars and beyond. To make electronics, you need chips, wafers, transistors, reticles, and... To make these, you must see, test and manufacture them at scale—faster and better than ever before. That's where KLA comes in. Whether you're early in your career or an experienced professional, you'll solve complex challenges, work alongside brilliant minds and help shape the future of technology.

Group/Division

The Semiconductor Products and Customers (Semi PC) business unit designs, builds and sells KLA’s product portfolio to help chip manufacturers meet high-quality standards for technologies like AI, data centers, automotive and electronic devices. Our inspection, metrology, and analytics systems detect and monitor defects across logic and memory chips, specialty semiconductors, wafers, reticles, advanced packaging, process equipment and materials. We also develop technologies for specialty processes, IC substrates, and PCB manufacturing, including etch and deposition, component inspection, and imaging and analytics. The RAPID division leads the industry in reticle inspection solutions, helping ensure high lithography yields and cost-effective semiconductor manufacturing. Its systems support both mask shops and fabs by detecting defects early in the process, enabling faster, more reliable production.

In this role, you will play a key part in advancing business priorities by delivering high-impact work across your area of expertise.

- Apply Machine Learning and Deep Learning techniques to image transformation and defect detection.
- Analyze large-scale image datasets and evaluate algorithm performance.
- Prototype algorithms using Python, PyTorch, and TensorFlow.
- Develop production-quality software using Modern C++ and Python.
- Apply best practices in software design, testing, debugging, code reviews, and version control.
- Collaborate with algorithm, software, systems, and application engineers to deploy solutions into production.

- Strong background in Computer Vision, Image Processing, Machine Learning, Deep Learning, or Pattern Recognition.
- Strong programming skills in C++ and/or Python.
- Familiarity with PyTorch, TensorFlow, or equivalent ML frameworks.

- Experience with CNNs, Vision Transformers, or segmentation models.
- Experience with Modern C++ software development.
- Knowledge of image enhancement, image registration, feature extraction, or anomaly detection.
- Experience with large-scale datasets and quantitative algorithm evaluation.

- Hands-on experience in AI, Computer Vision, Deep Learning, Image Processing, Modern C++, and Software Engineering.
- End-to-end exposure to algorithm development, optimization, and deployment.
- Experience building scalable, production-quality software.
- Mentorship from experts in algorithms, imaging, software engineering, and semiconductor inspection.

Pursuing a Ph.D. in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Applied Mathematics, Physics, Data Science, or a related field.

About Zipline

Zipline is the world’s largest and most experienced drone delivery service. We are on a mission to serve all humans equally by ensuring access to food, medicine and essential goods anytime, anywhere. We design, build, and operate the world’s largest autonomous logistics system, delivering critical supplies quickly and reliably. Today, Zipline operates on four continents, makes a delivery somewhere in the world every 30 seconds, and has completed millions of deliveries to date, including blood, vaccines, medical supplies, food, and retail products.

Our customers include the world’s largest and most prominent healthcare systems, governments, retailers, restaurants and global businesses who rely on us to save lives, reduce emissions, increase economic opportunity, and provide delivery from point A to point B as fast as possible. The drone is only 15% of what we’ve built to enable seamless, reliable, global operations.

Our system strengthens supply chains, reduces congestion, and gives people time back. With more than 140 million commercial autonomous miles safely flown, Zipline is redefining access to healthcare, consumer products, and food across the globe.

We operate at a global scale and are looking for practical problem solvers who thrive on real-world challenges and rapid growth. Our team is motivated by building systems that have a direct, meaningful impact on people’s lives and by scaling the future of logistics. We are seeking people who sculpt from first principles, enjoy facing adversity, and can do the impossible at record breaking speeds.

About the Real Estate & Development Team

The Real Estate & Development team identifies, secures, and entitles the sites that power Zipline’s network. We source markets, lead site selection and due diligence (zoning, utilities, environmental), negotiate LOIs/leases and land agreements, and drive entitlements and permitting with municipalities and partner real estate teams. We align stakeholders, manage budgets and schedules, and deliver permitted, ready-to-build locations—spanning test sites and regional hubs—before handing off to construction. By turning candidate properties into drone delivery sites at speed, we enable Zipline to scale into new regions and deliver life-changing logistics where they’re needed most.

The Role

As a Real Estate & Development Intern based in our San Francisco office, you will help expand the physical infrastructure that makes Zipline’s delivery system possible. You will support projects from early site identification through approvals and development, helping turn promising locations into operational sites that serve customers and communities. Along the way, you will tackle complex, real-world challenges at the intersection of aviation, real estate, technology, and the built environment. You will work alongside and learn from experienced partners across Real Estate, Engineering, Operations, Government Affairs, and Communications. Your work will contribute directly to Zipline’s mission by helping bring fast, reliable delivery to more people in more places.

What You'll Do

- Support market screening and site selection by evaluating zoning, land-use requirements, setbacks, utilities, easements, environmental conditions, and airspace considerations.

- Assess potential sites for feasibility and risk, identifying permitting hurdles, title issues, infrastructure constraints, and other factors that could affect development.

- Partner with Engineering and Operations to translate technical requirements into practical site criteria, scopes of work, site plans, and permit-ready materials.

- Learn how projects move through local approval processes by working with city planners, zoning officials, building departments, and external consultants.

- Coordinate with landlords, brokers, and real estate partners to evaluate site readiness and support negotiations, including letters of intent, leases, and required exhibits.

- Prepare comparative site analyses, deal memos, and recommendation summaries that help cross-functional teams make informed investment and development decisions.

- Build project-management skills by maintaining timelines, budget estimates, and entitlement trackers, communicating progress to stakeholders, and preparing complete handoff packages for downstream teams.

What You'll Bring

- Currently pursuing a bachelor’s or graduate degree in real estate, urban planning, engineering, construction management, architecture, geography, environmental studies, business, public policy, or a related field.

- Demonstrated interest in real estate development, site acquisition, infrastructure, permitting, or the built environment through coursework, projects, internships, or other relevant experience.

- Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, including the ability to evaluate information from multiple sources, identify potential risks, and form a clear recommendation.

- Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the judgment to work professionally with cross-functional teammates, consultants, property owners, and public-agency stakeholders.

- Strong organization and attention to detail, with the ability to manage multiple assignments, maintain accurate project information, and follow through on deadlines.

- Comfort learning new tools and working with maps, spreadsheets, plans, schedules, and project documentation; prior experience with specialized real estate, design, or construction software is not required.

What Else You Should Know

Our internships are full-time positions, in-person at our South San Francisco office. We will host our Summer 2027 interns from May/June to August/September.

Candidates are limited to three (3) applications within a 30-day period.

About the Team
Every TikTok video starts the same way: someone opens the camera. That moment — and everything that follows, from framing a shot to switching effects to hitting record — has to feel instant and effortless. We are the TikTok Camera Client Team, responsible for the experience and performance of the creation entry point used by hundreds of millions of people every day. Our mission is to make the camera fast to open, fluid to touch, and rock-solid on every device our users hold, from the latest flagship to the most entry-level phone. If you care about how an app actually feels in the hand, and about the engineering underneath that makes it feel that way, you came to the right place.

You will be working on two sides of the same problem. On the experience side, you'll help refine how creation feels — responsiveness of capture, smoothness of effect switching, gestures, and transitions — turning rough edges into flows that feel natural. On the performance side, you'll attack what quietly ruins that feeling at scale: slow cold start, jank, memory pressure, power drain, and stability issues on low-end devices. Partnering closely with product, design, and the effects and camera pipeline teams, you'll help build the tooling that makes this work measurable and repeatable. Small wins here are multiplied by hundreds of millions of daily creation sessions.

- Assist in the design and implementation of automated performance monitoring pipelines, such as automatic Perfetto trace capture, agent-assisted bottleneck analysis, and regression detection, to assess camera experience and performance at various stages
- Using client-side optimization techniques such as cold start optimization, jank and memory analysis, and thread scheduling to improve camera responsiveness and stability across a massive range of mobile devices

OVERVIEW

Imagine. With over 1,400 stores throughout the U.S. and a thriving supply chain network, there has never been a greater need for people of high initiative, big-picture thinking, and adaptability to share in our journey. At Ulta Beauty, we have greater ambitions. Growing what works. Iterating in areas that have promise. Creating new offerings for industry advantage.

Behind the thousands of beauty products and brands our guests discover every day is a complex supply chain connecting distribution centers, stores, digital channels, and teams across the organization. Data plays an important role in helping those teams understand performance, identify opportunities, and make better decisions.

For someone excited by both analytics and the beauty industry, this internship provides an opportunity to see how data and technology help bring the possibilities of beauty to life for our guests.

THE IMPACT YOU CAN HAVE:

As a Supply Chain Data & Analytics Intern, you will gain hands-on experience using data to support decision-making across Ulta Beauty's supply chain. Working alongside the Supply Chain Data & Analytics team, you will help transform data from Distribution Center (DC) Operations and Retail Operations into reporting, visualizations, and insights that improve visibility into supply chain performance.

You will have the opportunity to develop practical skills in SQL, data visualization, reporting, and analytics while learning how data moves from operational systems through transformation processes and ultimately into the dashboards and insights used by the business.

Throughout the internship, you will collaborate with analysts and business partners, contribute to existing analytics solutions, and work toward an end-to-end dashboard project that addresses a real Supply Chain business need that will be presented to Leadership teams. From understanding the business question and exploring the underlying data to developing the visualization and presenting the finished solution, this project will provide the opportunity to experience the analytics delivery lifecycle from beginning to end.

YOU'LL ACCOMPLISH THESE GOALS BY:

- Develop and enhance Power BI dashboards and data visualizations that provide visibility into key Supply Chain metrics and operational performance.

Your Team, Your Impact

Our team performs the electrical validation of custom Marvell ASICs built around high-speed Ethernet and PCIe IO, the silicon that powers modern data center infrastructure. - Debug unexpected results with your mentor and team until a solution is found.
- Build Python automation and AI-assisted validation agents, using tools such as Claude and Glean, to speed up daily routines.

- Currently pursuing a Bachelor’s Degree in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, or a related field with an expected graduation date between Fall 2027 – Summer 2028

28 - 56, $ per hour.

Security Clearance

None required. However, if your assignment is longer than 179 days cumulatively within a calendar year, you must go through the Personal Identity Verification process. This process includes completing an online background investigation form and receiving approval of the background check.

National Defense Authorization Act (NDAA)

The 2025 National Defense Authorization Act (NDAA), Section 3112, generally prohibits citizens of China, Russia, Iran and North Korea without dual US citizenship or legal permanent residence from accessing specific non-public areas of national security or nuclear weapons facilities. The restrictions of NDAA Section 3112 apply to this position. To be qualified for this position, Candidates must be eligible to access the Laboratory in compliance with Section 3112.

Pre-Employment Drug Test

External applicant(s) selected for this position must pass a post-offer, pre-employment drug test. This includes testing for use of marijuana as Federal Law applies to us as a Federal Contractor.

Wireless and Medical Devices

Per the Department of Energy (DOE), Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory must meet certain restrictions with the use and/or possession of mobile devices in Limited Areas. Depending on your job duties, you may be required to work in a Limited Area where you are not permitted to have a personal and/or laboratory mobile device in your possession. This includes, but not limited to cell phones, tablets, fitness devices, wireless headphones, and other Bluetooth/wireless enabled devices.

If you use a medical device, which pairs with a mobile device, you must still follow the rules concerning the mobile device in individual sections within Limited Areas. Sensitive Compartmented Information Facilities require separate approval. Hearing aids without wireless capabilities or wireless that has been disabled are allowed in Limited Areas, Secure Space and Transit/Buffer Space within buildings.

How to identify fake job advertisements

Please be aware of recruitment scams where people or entities are misusing the name of Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory (LLNL) to post fake job advertisements. LLNL never extends an offer without a personal interview and will never charge a fee for joining our company. All current job openings are displayed on the Career Page under “Find Your Job” of our website. If you have encountered a job posting or have been approached with a job offer that you suspect may be fraudulent, we strongly recommend you do not respond.

To learn more about recruitment scams: https://www.llnl.gov/sites/www/files/2023-05/LLNL-Job-Fraud-Statement-Updated-4.26.23.pdf

California Privacy Notice

About Zipline

Zipline is the world’s largest and most experienced drone delivery service. We are on a mission to serve all humans equally by ensuring access to food, medicine and essential goods anytime, anywhere. We design, build, and operate the world’s largest autonomous logistics system, delivering critical supplies quickly and reliably. Today, Zipline operates on four continents, makes a delivery somewhere in the world every 30 seconds, and has completed millions of deliveries to date, including blood, vaccines, medical supplies, food, and retail products.

Our customers include the world’s largest and most prominent healthcare systems, governments, retailers, restaurants and global businesses who rely on us to save lives, reduce emissions, increase economic opportunity, and provide delivery from point A to point B as fast as possible. The drone is only 15% of what we’ve built to enable seamless, reliable, global operations.

Our system strengthens supply chains, reduces congestion, and gives people time back. With more than 140 million commercial autonomous miles safely flown, Zipline is redefining access to healthcare, consumer products, and food across the globe.

We operate at a global scale and are looking for practical problem solvers who thrive on real-world challenges and rapid growth. Our team is motivated by building systems that have a direct, meaningful impact on people’s lives and by scaling the future of logistics. We are seeking people who sculpt from first principles, enjoy facing adversity, and can do the impossible at record breaking speeds.

About the Sales Operations Team

Sales Operations partners with Zipline’s commercial teams to turn strategy into repeatable execution. We build the systems, data, and operating rhythms that help sales teams prioritize the right accounts, manage pipeline, and act on insights. Our work spans CRM governance, account research, pipeline reporting, process improvement, sales enablement, and cross-functional go-to-market initiatives.

The Role

As a Sales Operations Analyst Intern, you will help strengthen the infrastructure behind Zipline’s growing commercial organization. You will work on projects that make sales data more useful, processes more scalable, and decisions easier to make. You may support pipeline analysis, account and territory planning, CRM improvements, prospecting operations, and reporting. You will collaborate with Sales, Marketing, Finance, and other business partners while learning how a high-growth company builds and scales its go-to-market engine.

What You'll Do

- Audit, standardize, and enrich CRM records to improve data quality and trust in reporting.

- Support recurring pipeline, forecast, and funnel reporting; identify trends in stage movement, aging, coverage, and conversion.

- Build account lists, market maps, and research briefs that help sales teams prioritize prospects and whitespace opportunities.

- Document and improve sales processes, including lead routing, handoffs, opportunity stages, and follow-up workflows.

- Coordinate cross-functional Sales Operations initiatives by tracking milestones, owners, risks, and next steps.

- Create practical dashboards, analysis, playbooks, and enablement materials for sales and leadership stakeholders.

- Identify repetitive work and help evaluate automation or AI-enabled ways to improve speed, consistency, and quality.

What You'll Bring

- You must have completed at least two years of undergraduate degree in business, economics, analytics, marketing, operations, engineering, or a related field. Candidates who are currently pursuing or have completed a bachelor’s, master’s, or MBA degree are eligible.

- Strong analytical, organizational, and problem-solving skills, with an ability to work carefully with data and details.

- Curiosity about how sales organizations operate and a willingness to ask questions, investigate problems, and learn new tools.

- Clear written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to turn analysis into a concise recommendation.

- Comfort managing multiple workstreams in a fast-moving and sometimes ambiguous environment.

- Experience with spreadsheets, CRM systems, reporting tools, or process documentation is helpful but not required.

- HubSpot Admin experience is a plus.

What Else You Should Know

This internship is a full-time position, in-person at our South San Francisco office. We will host our Summer 2027 interns from (May/June - August/September). Zipline is unable to sponsor work visas for applicants to this position.

The hourly rate for this internship is $40 per hour. Additional benefits may include relocation support, a housing stipend, overtime pay, paid sick time, and other benefits, where applicable and subject to local requirements.

Candidates are limited to three (3) applications within a 30-day period.

Zipline is an equal opportunity employer and prohibits discrimination and harassment of any type without regard to race, color, religion, age, sex, national origin, disability status, genetics, protected veteran status, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, or any other characteristic protected by federal, state or local laws or our own sensibilities.

Zipline is also committed to providing reasonable accommodations to individuals with disabilities. Please let your point of contact at Zipline know if you require any accommodations throughout your interview process.

Voluntary Self-Identification

WindBorne Systems is supercharging weather models with a unique proprietary data source: a global constellation of next-generation smart weather balloons targeting the most critical atmospheric data. We design, manufacture, and operate our own balloons, using the data they collect to generate otherwise unattainable weather intelligence.

Our mission is to eliminate weather uncertainty, and in the process help humanity adapt to climate change, be that predicting hurricanes or speeding the adoption of renewables. We are building a future in which the planet is instrumented by thousands of our microballoons, eliminating gaps in our understanding of the planet and giving people and businesses the information they need to make critical decisions. The founding team of Stanford engineers was named Forbes 2019 30 under 30 and is backed by top investors including Khosla Ventures.

WindBorne is looking for a Firmware Intern to build the code bases that runs on our balloon hardware. As a vertically integrated weather company, we design, calibrate, & integrate our own custom sensors & control mechanisms into our autonomous balloons. This poses some unique challenges: most components are outside their temperature spec, power is extremely limited and it is not easy to update code when the system is many miles in the air. We believe the most interesting work happens at the intersection of hardware and software, where clever code can compensate for physical limitations. In this role, you’ll design and run experiments to understand the behaviors of our system in weird conditions, then cosplay as a 1960s NASA engineer to glean insight from the limited data available. You’ll own firmware strategy, making quick, tactical decisions on whether to vomit some code for a janky test or design a robust solution that will accelerate future development. From maintaining our custom RTOS and hardware abstraction layer to developing the driver interfaces for our suite of atmospheric sensors, you'll be solving fascinating challenges alongside a team of brilliant, passionate engineers who are revolutionising our understanding of the atmosphere.

This role is open at any point, not just during the summer. Applications are considered on a rolling basis.

Responsibilities:

- Develop and maintain drivers & low level libraries for new chips, modules, & sensors

- Own our custom open source RTOS hardware abstraction layer, Amslah. It has many custom features made for our unique application (I’m excited to tell you about them!) but ​​but requires hardening and architecture refinements as we scale

- Push the limits of our custom sensor hardware & calibration infrastructure, ensuring our GSBs are power optimized & survive extreme cold beyond subcomponent specifications.

- Work closely with people doing R&D on novel hardware as we seek to improve the accuracy of our meteorological measurements.

- Design fault-tolerant systems that can recover gracefully from unexpected conditions

- Debug highly non-trivial issues

Skills and Qualifications:

- Experience programming, shipping, and maintaining hardware in a real-world setting.

- Must be excited by rapid iteration more than trying to perfectly plan ahead of time

- Fluent in C/C++ and Python. Though ideally you ever so slightly look down on software engineers who only write interpreted languages, but you wouldn’t admit this because you are too nice.

- Should have experience writing low-level drivers for a number of various chips.

- Should be comfortable reading PCB schematics. Ideally have done a bit of EE yourself :)

- Be able to form hypothesis and run experiments about the behaviour of the system

- Must be an effective communicator, able to cut through misunderstandings to the core of an issue and reason about tradeoffs in complex multidisciplinary spaces

- Excellent debugging skills in complex settings

Nice to have:

- Experience with FPGAs and HDL

- Knowledge of RF systems and wireless protocols

- Degree in Computer Science/Electrical Engineering or related field

- Stellar understanding of undergrad level physics

Salary

- $33/hr

Location

1600 Bridge Pwky, Redwood City, CA. In person required.

OpenGov is on a mission to power a more effective and accountable government — and the software our engineering teams ship every day makes that real for thousands of public agencies across the country. As a Software Engineering Intern, you'll contribute to production features used by real customers, working side by side with full-time engineers across the full stack. Expect to leave with a deeper understanding of how modern SaaS engineering teams build, test, and deliver enterprise-grade software at scale.

- Build and ship features across our production codebase, contributing to web applications and APIs that serve government customers every day

- Design, document, and implement REST API endpoints in collaboration with senior engineers, learning how scalable service contracts are built and maintained

- Write unit and integration tests alongside feature work, developing habits around code quality and test coverage from day one

- Participate in code reviews — both receiving and giving feedback — to sharpen your craft and understand how the team maintains a high bar for quality

- Collaborate with engineers during sprint planning, standups, and retrospectives to experience the full rhythm of an agile engineering team

- Investigate and resolve bugs and performance issues, tracing problems through the stack to develop debugging instincts in a real production environment

- Explore AI-assisted development tools to accelerate your workflow and get exposure to how modern engineering teams are integrating AI into their day-to-day

Requirements and Preferred Experience

Requirements:

- Currently pursuing a Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, or a related field, or equivalent program

- Proficiency in at least one modern programming language (TypeScript, JavaScript, React, or Node)

- Experience building with AI-driven UX, agents, and workflow automation (direct ML experience not required)

- Ability to collaborate effectively in a team environment and communicate clearly about technical problems

- Strong problem-solving skills and attention to detail — you spot edge cases and ask good questions

- Curiosity and a self-starter mindset; eager to learn from feedback and iterate quickly

Preferred Experience:

- Familiarity with front-end frameworks such as Angular, React, or Redux

- Basic experience with Git or similar version control tools

- Personal or open-source projects you're proud of — GitHub link welcome

- Strong written or verbal communication skills; bonus if you've shared your work via blogs, talks, or demos

- GPA 3.0+

Compensation:

Boston, MA: $30 per hour

On target ranges above include base plus a portion of variable compensation that is earned based on company and individual performance.

The final compensation will be determined by a number of factors such as qualifications, expertise, and the candidate’s geographical location.

Why OpenGov?

A Mission That Matters.

At OpenGov, public service is personal. We are passionate about our mission to power more effective and accountable government. Government that operates efficiently, adapts to change, and strengthens public trust. Some people say this is boring. We think it’s the core of our democracy.

Opportunity to Innovate
